svg.title: Resolution of two point sources: the Rayleigh criterion
svg.desc: Three intensity profiles, each the sum of two Airy diffraction patterns from two point sources. At 1.5 times the Rayleigh distance the two peaks are clearly separate; at the Rayleigh distance d = 0.61 lambda / NA the sum dips to 74 percent between the peaks; at half the Rayleigh distance the profile has a single peak.
svg.text: When are two points resolved? The Rayleigh criterion
Each point source images as an Airy pattern (dashed); the microscope records their sum (solid).
Rayleigh distance d = 0.61 λ / NA: the peak of one pattern falls on the first dark ring of the other.
Triangles mark the true positions of the two points. Profiles computed from the Airy function [2 J1(v)/v]² (code in the Microscopy note).
